schema_rules: No IP addresses or host names of launch servers.
No private keys, seeds or secrets.
No names of root key holders; holders are kit holder 1 to 5.
Attack results are counts and pass or fail only; details follow only after a fix.
Evidence links point only to github.com/DytallixHQ/dytallix.

phases.name: Simulation plan
phases.summary: The seven runs, their pass criteria, timings, host access, load source and the statistical campaign, approved as one decision record.

phases.name: Simulation tools
phases.summary: Nine tools (T1 to T9) that build rehearsal genesis, drive the hosts, generate load and attacks, inject faults and record evidence. Each is proven in the CI staging network first.

phases.name: Staging on production hosts
phases.summary: The two production hosts, the validator and the sentry, run the peer tests, the capacity measurements and the root kit drills with rehearsal identities.

phases.name: Statistical campaign
phases.summary: Thousands of attack attempts per type, repeated faults and an endurance run of at least 15 days, so results carry statistical confidence.

phases.name: Freeze, audit and public review
phases.summary: The release candidate is frozen, audited by Hashlock and opened to a 30-day public review with a DGT bug bounty. Every finding is fixed or answered on the record.

phases.name: Seven launch simulations
phases.summary: Seven full launches (R01 to R07) on the final candidate, each from clean hosts and a fresh rehearsal genesis, each operating for 24 hours.

phases.name: Dress rehearsal checkpoints
phases.summary: R07 follows the exact production launch procedure, with checks from six hours before genesis to 24 hours after.

phases.name: Genesis
phases.summary: The final inputs are frozen, the release and genesis are reproduced byte for byte, three of five root kits sign, and the founder signs off.

groups.name: Governance

groups.name: Performance
groups.summary: Block intervals, inclusion delay and response times over the endurance run.

groups.name: Endurance
groups.summary: At least 15 days continuous at the exact production values.

groups.name: Release freeze
groups.summary: The candidate under review.

groups.name: Hashlock audit
groups.summary: Independent security audit of the frozen candidate.

groups.name: Public review
groups.summary: 30 days with a DGT bug bounty.

groups.name: Clean genesis
groups.summary: The full launch with rehearsal identities: genesis, wallets, staking, transfers, fees and rewards, with supply reconciled at each checkpoint.

groups.name: Infrastructure failure
groups.summary: Process kills, the sentry stopped and restored, a destroyed sentry, a network cut and a lost validator host, each recovered and checked.

groups.name: Adversarial network
groups.summary: Latency, packet loss, a partition, malformed and invalid transactions and request floods from outside machines.

groups.name: Production upgrade
groups.summary: A signed release handover and state upgrade from one candidate to the next, with state checked before and after.

groups.name: Operator error
groups.summary: Wrong configuration, binary, network, genesis, peers and versions, and a second copy of the validator key. Each must be refused or harmless.

groups.name: Load and economic activity
groups.summary: 1,000 wallets, sustained load at full and half capacity, staking, governance and malformed traffic mixed in.

groups.name: Final dress rehearsal
groups.summary: The exact production launch procedure with production values, from six hours before genesis to 24 hours after.

groups.name: Six hours before
groups.summary: Binaries, genesis, allocations, supply, validators, infrastructure, monitoring and backups.

groups.name: One hour before
groups.summary: Genesis and binary hashes, peers, clocks, keys, configuration and parameters.

groups.name: Genesis
groups.summary: Start, consensus, block production and validator participation.

groups.name: Fifteen minutes after
groups.summary: RPC, wallets, a PQC transaction, DRT and DGT transfers, a delegation, fees and finality.

groups.name: One hour after
groups.summary: State consistency across nodes, wallets, staking, rewards, supply and monitoring.

groups.name: Six hours after
groups.summary: Telemetry, logs, participation, accounting, transactions, alerts and staking.

groups.name: 24 hours after
groups.summary: Full supply reconciliation, validator review and final state review.

groups.name: Input freeze
groups.summary: Allocation ledger and genesis time.

groups.name: Reproduction
groups.summary: Release and genesis rebuilt independently.

groups.name: Root signatures
groups.summary: Three of five kits sign the genesis.

kpis.name: Negative peer tests
kpis.measures: Wrong-key, malformed and unexpected peers against the production hosts' post-quantum transport.
kpis.why: Only approved peers may reach the validator. A peer that should be refused must be refused.

kpis.name: Measured capacity
kpis.measures: Basic transfers per block the hosts sustain within the approved queue and connection limits.
kpis.why: The load thresholds in R06 depend on a capacity measured on the real hosts, not estimated.
kpis.threshold: Confirms about 180 basic Sends a block

kpis.name: Root kit drill
kpis.measures: Three of five rehearsal kits prepare, sign and submit a root control end to end.
kpis.why: Upgrades and emergency controls need three kit holders acting together. The procedure is rehearsed before it is needed.

kpis.name: Transactions: attempts
kpis.measures: Attempts made per attack type. Covers: Invalid, wrong-key and truncated ML-DSA-65 signatures; malformed and oversized envelopes; wrong chain; expired, stale and conflicting nonces; duplicates; fee caps below the minimum; overspending.
kpis.why: At least 3,000 attempts with zero successes bounds the success rate below 1 in 1,000 at 95% confidence (rule of three).

kpis.name: Transactions: successes
kpis.measures: Attempts that the chain accepted or that changed state when it should not have.
kpis.why: Any success is a defect, fixed before the release freeze. Details are published only after the fix.

kpis.name: Validator restart
kpis.measures: Time from a validator process restart to the next committed block. The chain has one validator, so it pauses meanwhile. About 30 repetitions; recorded as a distribution.
kpis.why: Recovery targets are what users can expect from a one-validator launch. Repeated measurement shows the spread, not one lucky run.
kpis.threshold: Blocks again within 5 minutes, every time

kpis.name: Network heal
kpis.measures: Time for the sentry to catch up after a network cut is restored. About 30 repetitions; recorded as a distribution.
kpis.why: Recovery targets are what users can expect from a one-validator launch. Repeated measurement shows the spread, not one lucky run.
kpis.threshold: Caught up within 2 minutes, every time

kpis.name: Sentry rebuild
kpis.measures: Time to rebuild a destroyed sentry, the public node, from its snapshot. 3 to 5 repetitions; recorded as a distribution.
kpis.why: Recovery targets are what users can expect from a one-validator launch. Repeated measurement shows the spread, not one lucky run.

kpis.name: Validator host recovery
kpis.measures: Time to recover a lost validator host by the fence-first procedure. 3 to 5 repetitions; recorded as a distribution.
kpis.why: Recovery targets are what users can expect from a one-validator launch. Repeated measurement shows the spread, not one lucky run.

kpis.name: Fault alerts
kpis.measures: Injected faults that raised their alert and resolved it after recovery.
kpis.why: The founder runs the chain alone. An outage that does not alert can last until someone notices.

kpis.name: Block interval, median
kpis.measures: Seconds between consecutive committed blocks, outside injected faults. A day gives about 17,280 blocks.
kpis.why: Block interval is how long a user waits for a transaction to be final. The tail matters as much as the median.

kpis.name: Block interval, 95th percentile
kpis.measures: Seconds between consecutive committed blocks, outside injected faults. A day gives about 17,280 blocks.
kpis.why: Block interval is how long a user waits for a transaction to be final. The tail matters as much as the median.

kpis.name: Block interval, 99th percentile
kpis.measures: Seconds between consecutive committed blocks, outside injected faults. A day gives about 17,280 blocks.
kpis.why: Block interval is how long a user waits for a transaction to be final. The tail matters as much as the median.

kpis.name: Block interval, 99.9th percentile
kpis.measures: Seconds between consecutive committed blocks, outside injected faults. A day gives about 17,280 blocks.
kpis.why: Block interval is how long a user waits for a transaction to be final. The tail matters as much as the median.

kpis.name: Inclusion at half capacity
kpis.measures: Valid transactions committed within 2 blocks of submission while the chain runs at half capacity.
kpis.why: Shows that ordinary transactions are not delayed or dropped under normal load.

kpis.name: Client response time, 99th percentile
kpis.measures: Time for the public node to answer a client request, under background load.
kpis.why: Wallets and applications reach the chain only through the public node. Slow answers look like an outage to users.

kpis.name: Endurance run
kpis.measures: Continuous days at the exact production values with background load, covering full unbonding, governance voting and a release handover.
kpis.why: Some lifecycles take two weeks at production values. Slow leaks in state or memory only show over time.

kpis.name: Epochs and snapshots
kpis.measures: Reward epochs and state snapshots completed during the endurance run.
kpis.why: Emission, rewards and snapshot restore are checked across many boundaries, not one.

kpis.name: Release candidate frozen
kpis.measures: A tagged release candidate whose binaries a clean CI runner and a fresh container reproduce byte for byte.
kpis.why: The audit, the public review and the simulations must all test the same code.

kpis.name: Independent audit
kpis.measures: Hashlock's audit of the consensus application, the post-quantum CometBFT fork, the root authorization tools and the CLI wallet.
kpis.why: An independent human audit lowers the risk of defects. The launch is labeled unaudited until the report is published.
kpis.threshold: Report published; every finding fixed and re-checked, or answered on the record

kpis.name: Public review
kpis.measures: Days the frozen candidate has been open to public review with a DGT bug bounty.
kpis.why: Anyone can inspect the code before it holds value, and reports are rewarded.

kpis.name: Open findings
kpis.measures: Audit, public review and AI review findings not yet fixed or answered on the record.
kpis.why: No finding may be silently dropped before launch.

kpis.name: AI review
kpis.measures: An adversarial review by an AI model of the candidate's code, published and labeled as AI.
kpis.why: It adds coverage, but it is not independent human review, and it is never presented as one.

kpis.name: R01 integrity
kpis.measures: Conflicting finalized blocks, app hashes on every node at every checkpoint, supply reconciliation (DRT genesis plus emitted minus burned, DGT unchanged) and blocks lost in recovery.
kpis.why: Safety first: a conflicting block or an unexplained supply difference stops the run.
kpis.threshold: Zero conflicts; one app hash; exact supply; no committed block lost

kpis.name: R01 liveness
kpis.measures: Median and 99th percentile block interval outside injected faults.
kpis.why: Shows the chain keeps a steady pace during the whole operating period.
kpis.threshold: Median at most 6 s; 99th percentile at most 10 s

kpis.name: R01 inclusion
kpis.measures: Valid transactions committed within 2 blocks at half capacity, and transactions lost at full capacity.
kpis.why: A valid transaction must be committed or refused at admission, never silently lost.
kpis.threshold: 99% within 2 blocks at half capacity; none lost at full

kpis.name: R01 recovery
kpis.measures: Time to recover from each injected fault, and whether each fault raised its alert and resolved.
kpis.why: Faults are certain over time; the targets bound how long users wait.

kpis.name: R01 load
kpis.measures: Full capacity, about 180 basic Sends a block, held for 1 hour, then half capacity for 6 hours, across 1,000 wallets.
kpis.why: Shows the production hosts sustain launch demand with the real fee and signature costs.

kpis.name: R07 liveness
kpis.measures: Median and 99th percentile block interval outside injected faults.
kpis.why: Shows the chain keeps a steady pace during the whole operating period.
kpis.threshold: Median at most 6 s; 99th percentile at most 10 s

kpis.name: R07 inclusion
kpis.measures: Valid transactions committed within 2 blocks at half capacity, and transactions lost at full capacity.
kpis.why: A valid transaction must be committed or refused at admission, never silently lost.
kpis.threshold: 99% within 2 blocks at half capacity; none lost at full

kpis.name: R07 recovery
kpis.measures: Time to recover from each injected fault, and whether each fault raised its alert and resolved.
kpis.why: Faults are certain over time; the targets bound how long users wait.

kpis.name: R07 load
kpis.measures: Full capacity, about 180 basic Sends a block, held for 1 hour, then half capacity for 6 hours, across 1,000 wallets.
kpis.why: Shows the production hosts sustain launch demand with the real fee and signature costs.

kpis.name: T-6h checks
kpis.measures: Verify binaries. Verify checksums. Verify release commit. Verify genesis. Verify all genesis allocations. Verify DRT supply. Verify DGT supply. Verify validators. Verify validator keys. Verify infrastructure. Verify networking. Verify DNS. Verify RPC. Verify monitoring. Verify alerts. Verify backups. Verify recovery procedures.
kpis.why: The dress rehearsal follows the exact launch procedure, so the real launch repeats steps that have already passed.

kpis.name: T-1h checks
kpis.measures: Confirm validator coordination. Confirm genesis hash. Confirm binary hash. Confirm peers. Confirm system clocks. Confirm validator keys. Confirm configuration. Confirm token allocations. Confirm network parameters.
kpis.why: The dress rehearsal follows the exact launch procedure, so the real launch repeats steps that have already passed.

kpis.name: T0 checks
kpis.measures: Start validators. Confirm consensus. Confirm block production. Verify expected validator participation.
kpis.why: The dress rehearsal follows the exact launch procedure, so the real launch repeats steps that have already passed.

kpis.name: T+15m checks
kpis.measures: Verify RPC. Verify wallet connectivity. Execute canonical PQC transaction. Execute DRT transaction. Execute DGT transaction. Create delegation. Verify fee accounting. Verify finalization.
kpis.why: The dress rehearsal follows the exact launch procedure, so the real launch repeats steps that have already passed.

kpis.name: T+1h checks
kpis.measures: Verify state consistency across validators. Verify wallets. Verify staking. Verify rewards. Verify token supply. Verify monitoring. Verify RPC infrastructure.
kpis.why: The dress rehearsal follows the exact launch procedure, so the real launch repeats steps that have already passed.

kpis.name: T+6h checks
kpis.measures: Review telemetry. Review logs. Review validator participation. Review token accounting. Review transaction statistics. Review security alerts. Review staking activity.
kpis.why: The dress rehearsal follows the exact launch procedure, so the real launch repeats steps that have already passed.

kpis.name: T+24h checks
kpis.measures: Perform full supply reconciliation. Perform full validator review. Perform final state consistency review.
kpis.why: The dress rehearsal follows the exact launch procedure, so the real launch repeats steps that have already passed.

kpis.name: Final input freeze
kpis.measures: The allocation ledger (buckets, holder grants, validator self-bond, DRT bootstrap) and the genesis time.
kpis.why: Genesis is reproducible only if every input is fixed and published first.
kpis.threshold: Frozen and published; genesis a weekday at 14:00 UTC, at least 72 h after the final build

kpis.name: Reproduced byte for byte
kpis.measures: Release and genesis digests built independently on a clean CI runner and a fresh container.
kpis.why: Anyone can check that the published binaries and genesis come from the published source.

kpis.name: Genesis signatures
kpis.measures: Root key kits that signed the genesis.
kpis.why: No one person, and no two, can sign the genesis alone.
